article_text:
Anyone shopping for a Yoshitomo Nara in New York this month has an embarrassment of riches. David Zwirner has filled two Chelsea galleries with the Japanese artist’s paintings. On opening night in Chelsea last week, hours-long lines stretched like highway caravans down 19th and 20th streets, leading to a deluge of posts similarly clogging up the art world’s Instagram feed. The shows have drawings, sculptures, and large new canvases priced as high as $6 million. But bring your checkbook and you might still be out of luck: One source familiar with the exhibition said the largest paintings are being held exclusively for museums.

A few blocks away, Loïc Gouzer’s Fair Warning is offering In the Milky Lake / Thinking One (2011), a monumental painting of a little girl standing waist-deep in pale water, her eyes lowered. Made in the year of the devastating Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami in northeastern Japan, where Nara grew up, the painting has appeared in major retrospectives around the world. It carries a $10–$15 million estimate for Fair Warning’s November 19 auction.

There are more Naras to be had: Sotheby’s is offering Candy Blue Night (2001) at The Now and Contemporary Sale next week with a $5–$7 million estimate, while Christie’s will send Miss Forest / Dark Night (2016), a bronze sculpture estimated at $1 million to $1.5 million, to the block at the 21st Century Evening Sale.

Nara’s auction record of $24.95 million was set at Sotheby’s Hong Kong in 2019. Although he hasn’t come close to $20 million since—at auction, anyways—his largest paintings have continued to sell for roughly $5 million to $15 million, even in a challenging market.

The works on offer this season are hardly interchangeable. In age, scale, medium, and importance, they are all different. But the sheer number of options gives us a snapshot of the art market during New York’s first official Art Week and as the November marquee sales draw near. Collectors can buy from galleries, bid at auction, or wait to see what happens before doing either.

That last option is becoming more and more attractive.

“The market’s healthy, but it continues to be measured with a certain amount of awareness, if not suspicion, about the aggressiveness of private pricing,” Alex Glauber , an art advisor and president of the Association of Professional Art Advisors, told ARTnews .

When collectors find a work at a gallery with a comparable example coming up at auction, Glauber said, more than a few prefer to wait for the result before committing. Unless the opportunity is particularly compelling or fleeting, buyers are taking their time.

It’s an awkward situation for dealers, who have spent months preparing exhibitions that open around the same time collectors flock into town for the evening sales. Art Week NYC , a citywide festival organized by ARTnews , Art in America , and Artforum and running today through Saturday, adds another reason to make the rounds. The galleries have certainly given collectors plenty to look at.

At Gagosian’s West 24th Street spaces, two exhibitions opening just days apart could hardly be more different. Julie Curtiss’s “UNREAL,” which opened Tuesday, gives a compellingly surreal vision of New York life. In Makeover (2026), two women in fur coats and sunglasses—Upper East Side types, if you ask me—wear post-op face masks. In other works, an elephant backs into a bodega, and a couple’s legs appear between washing machines. It’s all a bit naughty, in the best way. The paintings are priced roughly between $100,000 and $300,000, according to two sources familiar with the show.

Curtiss’s auction record of $466,000 was set at Phillips in 2021, amid a white-hot pandemic-era market for wet paint. Her market has cooled considerably since then: according to data from ARTDAI, her top result in the past two years was $115,000, achieved at Sotheby’s in May for a painting similar in size to the one sold in 2021.

Two doors down, on Thursday, Gagosian will open “Meine Schule,” an exhibition of Georg Baselitz ‘s final paintings and sculptures. The paintings, priced from around $1.5 million to $2.5 million, include upside-down images of the artist and his wife, Elke, drawn in thin black lines against gold backgrounds, with thick bursts of color. Two others return to his childhood in wartime Germany, showing schoolchildren holding hands beneath a Nazi banner.

We’ve seen this stuff before, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t great. The show’s most affecting work may be Strawinsky (2026), a large, white-patinated bronze figure seated with its head hanging forward and limbs collapsing around its body. The sculpture, priced at around $3 million, grew out of Baselitz’s designs for a marionette production of Stravinsky’s The Soldier’s Tale .

During a walkthrough, Stefan Ratibor, a director with the gallery, remembered visiting Baselitz at his studio outside Munich as the artist, working from a wheelchair, directed the final adjustments to the wooden model. Baselitz signed off on the sculpture and died the following night.

The story lends weight to this show as the last that he selected and designed. It also presents Gagosian with a very different commercial proposition from Curtiss: the final works of a major postwar artist whose output is now finite.

In SoHo, Hauser & Wirth has opened Rashid Johnson ‘s “Birthday Boys,” on the heels of his major Guggenheim retrospective last year. Five large mosaics made from ceramic tile, mirrors, oyster shells, and other materials depict fractured, doubled figures. They are priced from $750,000 to $1.2 million, according to a gallery price list I was able to get my hands on. (A similar work from 2021, Untitled Broken Crowd , sold for $1.27 million at Christie’s London in June.) A four-and-a-half-minute film about fathers and sons, which has the awkward, endearing quality of Wes Anderson sans the color saturation or the tweeness, is priced at $200,000.

At Skarstedt, Eric Fischl’s “In Pursuit of Pleasure,” opening Thursday, has 13 paintings of people enjoying, or at least attempting to enjoy, their leisure time. There are dog walkers, sunbathers, and yoga enthusiasts, often looking rather isolated despite the company around them. Two large paintings, Goat Yoga and Polished, Professional , are priced at $800,000 each, while Dog Walker is $425,000. Several other works are already marked reserved on the gallery’s price list.

Sean Kelly, meanwhile, is showing Kehinde Wiley’s portraits of New Yorkers, priced from about $100,000 to $400,000. That range is broadly in line with Wiley’s secondary-market prices, according to ARTDAI, though two outlier results have topped it: $649,000 in 2021 and $838,000 in 2024.

It bears mentioning that this is Wiley’s first show in New York since he was accused of sexual assault in 2024, allegations he has denied, and it may serve as something of a trial balloon for whether New York collectors are ready to embrace him as before. That may also be the thinking behind Christie’s and Sotheby’s decisions to offer Wiley portraits in their upcoming contemporary day sales. The Christie’s work, a double portrait of Nelly Moudime and Najaee Hall, carries an estimate of $150,000 to $200,000, while the Sotheby’s lot, depicting an unnamed male figure, has an estimate of $80,000 to $120,000.

Together, the exhibitions offer collectors a range of possibilities well beyond the eight-figure trophies dominating the auction headlines.

Other galleries are taking a less overtly commercial approach. Almine Rech is presenting James Turrell, Greene Naftali has Lubaina Himid, and White Cube is opening a major installation by Doris Salcedo. At 125 Newbury, Mark Rothko and Adolph Gottlieb are paired in an exhibition examining their Surrealist years.

Perhaps the clearest example is Lévy Gorvy Dayan’s exhibition of Francis Bacon and Willem de Kooning. The show is not selling anything. Instead, it brings together works by two postwar giants, demonstrating the sort of scholarship and access that can attract collectors even when there are no prices to negotiate. Rule No. 1 of sales: Get them in the door.

For all the activity, Glauber thinks the traditional May and November auction seasons have become somewhat less important to primary-market galleries than they were during the market’s hotter years. Auction houses have also backed off their onetime emphasis on emerging artists, which has smoothed the friction that came about when a young artist’s work came to auction while a gallery was still trying to establish primary-market prices.

Still, the basic tension remains. A private sale requires only one willing buyer. A strong auction result generally needs competing bidders, making the public sales an imperfect but useful test of demand.

For collectors considering the Naras scattered across Manhattan, that means plenty of opportunities to compare prices, quality, and availability. For dealers, it means making the case that their work is worth buying now, rather than waiting for the next hammer to fall.
excerpt_original: With millions of dollars in art on offer at galleries across New York, collectors have plenty of choices ahead of the November auctions. But increasingly, they're willing to wait.

article_text:
Feature

This Year's Gay Halloween Celebrates Women's Rights and Wrongs

From the Kelly Clarkson's mechanical bird fiasco to Carrie Bradshaw's Dior newsprint dress, Gay Halloween speaks to the staying power of women's iconic media moments.

Hyperallergic via

X )

With everything that's happened in the 1,000+ lifetimes jammed into 2026, I think we've all been waiting for Gay Halloween to rehash the year in popular culture. A recently named phenomenon for the chronically online, Gay Halloween is best described as the costume-based valorization of specific media moments, however iconic, niche, or overlooked they may be.

Against the grain of sexy cat costumes and run-of-the-mill superheroes, those blessed with ✨ the vision ✨ devote their resources and talents to fashioning a high-commitment outfit about some bullshit like the hyperpigmentation meme or the disco testicles stage prop from Kacey Musgraves's concert tour.

Hyperallergic via

X )

This year, I've noticed that a majority of Gay Halloween costumes pay homage to the real and fictional women carrying pop culture on their backs. That's not to say that there haven't been hat tips to the cyclosporiasis outbreak from Taylor Farms's lettuce, the hidden death rumors that emerged from Mitch McConnell's multi-week disappearance, or other 2026 happenings that were so absurd they became memes.

I'm just saying that for the most part, this year's Gay Halloween appears to be heavily influenced by the staying power of iconic women and their enduring impact across fashion history, viral interview clips, cringeworthy plot points, salacious scandals, and diva-defined media personas. And it gets really specific, too.

Hyperallergic via

X )

Negret）将担任本片导演。XYZ article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Michael Peña and Emmy nominee Anthony Ramos are set to star in Free Agent , a new thriller reteaming the producers and Oscar-winning writers of BlacKkKlansman .

Script is by Charlie Wachtel and David Rabinowitz , who after telling the story of Ron Stallworth, the African American police officer who infiltrated the Ku Klux Klan, have set their sights on another gripping true-life tale, reteaming with Shaun Redick and Yvette Yates Redick of Impossible Dream Entertainment , who are producing alongside Roberto Urbina, Jason Cherubini, and Martin Ramos of Colombia’s Synestesys.

Related Stories

Anthony Ramos Signs With UTA

Paul Walter Hauser, Boyd Holbrook & Michael Peña Among New Additions To Craig Zobel Thriller 'Turpentine'

Free Agent tells the story of sports agent Bartolo “Bart” Hernandez (Peña) and his unlikely partner Julio Estrada (Ramos), whose mission to help Cuba’s greatest athletes pursue the American Dream plunged them into an international world of organized crime, corruption, and the volatile politics between Cuba and the United States.

Watch on Deadline

Cuban-born Hernandez has lived baseball his whole life. A full-scholarship standout at McNeese State University, he was drafted by the Montreal Expos (now the Washington Nationals) before becoming a certified MLBPA agent. When signing Cuban talent became one of the most politically charged deals in sports, Hernandez was the agent at the center of it, landing record contracts for players who became MLB impact stars, including two Rookies of the Year and an MVP.

Hernandez’s story made national headlines when he and Estrada were convicted on conspiracy and alien smuggling charges in Miami federal court, revealing the dangerous lengths Cuban athletes and those helping them would go to in pursuit of the American Dream. Having served his time, Hernandez is back doing what he does best: representing, coaching, and training the next generation of big-league talent.

Free Agent began as a spec from Wachtel and Rabinowitz titled Bolsa Negra , which made the 2018 Black List.

Wachtel said, “This is a story we’ve been dying to share with the world. It’s an underdog tale about immigration, freedom, and the meaning – and cost – of the American Dream. We believe Bart’s incredible story has the unique potential to resonate across cultures and borders.”

Antonio Negret , a Colombian filmmaker who’s worked on shows like The Lincoln Lawyer and directed a number of features, takes the reins as director here. XYZ Films is exec producing the film and handling global sales, co-repping domestic rights with Impossible Dream Entertainment, whose Shaun Redick told us, “Collaborating with Charlie and David on BlacKkKlansman was one of the great experiences of my career, and I’ve been hoping for the right story to team up again. FREE AGENT is it. Just as they did with Ron Stallworth in BlacKkKlansman , they’ve found in Bart Hernandez a remarkable real-life character whose story is as riveting and wildly entertaining as it is inspiring. It’s the kind of story you can’t believe is true.”

Yvette Yates Redick added, “Working with Michael Peña and Anthony Ramos on FREE AGENT is a dream come true. They’re two of the most talented, charismatic actors working today, and as a Latina producer, it means so much to see them bring this story to life.”

Peña joins after work on Gore Verbinski’s Good Luck, Have Fun, Don’t Die , A Working Man opposite Jason Statham, and Peacock’s All Her Fault . Upcoming, he has the Amazon films Subversion and Judgment Day , plus the starry indies Tumor and Turpentine . He is repped by Entertainment 360, CAA, and Rick Genow of GGSSC.

Coming off roles in Ryan Murphy’s FX series The Beauty and The Shards , Ramos is repped by UTA, Range Media Partners, and Paul Hastings.

Negret is repped by Range Media Partners, Paradigm, and Feig Finkel; Wachtel and Rabinowitz by WME, Brillstein, and Behr Abramson Levy; and Impossible Dream Entertainment by Raskin Gorham Anderson Law. Production and finance legal is being handled by Gary Raskin and Dustin Sloan of Raskin Gorham Anderson Law and Stephanie Avalos of Andersen Law.

article_text:
ピアノ音楽における「エチュード（練習曲）」は、演奏技術を磨くための楽曲であり、ときに演奏者の技術的な限界に挑むものだ。フロレンティーナ・ホルツィンガーが ヴェネチア・ビエンナーレ での最後の パフォーマンス に冠したタイトル《CLOSING ÉTUDE》も、こうした挑戦を思わせる。7カ月にわたって展開してきた《SEAWORLD VENICE》は、身体表現や廃棄物を用いた インスタレーション を通じて、既存の規範に挑んできた。その最終章となる今回のパフォーマンスもまた、過酷な試みとなる。

パフォーマンスとインスタレーションを組み合わせた《SEAWORLD VENICE》は、5月に オーストリア 館で開幕した。 ヴェネチア の潟湖から引き揚げられた巨大な鐘が鋭い音を響かせるなか、ホルツィンガーは裸身で、鐘の内側で揺れて音を鳴らす「舌」の役割を担った。身体を張った過激な表現を通じて人間の身体の限界を探る彼女の実践の一端だ。ホルツィンガーが不在の間も鐘は毎正時に鳴り続け、来場者に時を告げる。それは、水没の危機に直面するヴェネチアの未来を暗示するグロテスクな祭壇のようだ。

インスタレーションには、人間の排泄物と潟湖の廃棄物が素材として用いられている。後者には、高潮とともに岸辺に打ち寄せられるゴミなども含まれる。会場には、来場者が利用できる仮設トイレが設置されており、そこで集められた尿は濾過された後、人が水に落ちる仕掛けを備えた装置「ダンクタンク」に送られる仕組みだ。

最後のパフォーマンスの《CLOSING ÉTUDE》において、儀式的な行進とともに鐘はオーストリア館を出発し、ヴェネチアのカンナレージョ地区にある歴史的建造物、スクオーラ・グランデ・デッラ・ミゼリコルディアへと運ばれる。同建物は、中世に同業者組合の施設として設立され、修復を経て2015年に展示スペースとして再開した。高くそびえる天井と広大な空間、パオロ・ヴェロネーゼの工房に帰属するとされるフレスコ画は、鐘の存在感と、ホルツィンガーが作品に込めた 宗教 的な雰囲気を際立たせる。《CLOSING ÉTUDE》は、 キリスト の「最後の晩餐」を想起させる「最後のディナー」と位置づけられている。

発表によると、《CLOSING ÉTUDE》では、物質が固体から液体へと変化する過程をたどり、聖遺物を生み出すという。過去7カ月間に、パビリオンの仮設トイレ利用者から集められたすべての排泄物を含む蒸留残留物は、未来に向けた記念碑として、最終日となる11月22日に閉館後のパビリオン前で公開される。鐘が「沈黙」し、水の「循環が止まる」とき、この展示は幕を閉じるというわけだ。

ただし、《SEAWORLD VENICE》の展開はこれで終わりではない。同作を再構成したバージョンが、来春には ベルリン のグロピウス・バウで、同年秋にはウィーンのクンストハレ・ウィーンで発表される予定だ。さらに、2028年3月には ブルックリン のアマントでも展示が予定されている。

こうした再構成バージョンの監修を務めるのは、ヴェネチアでの展示を企画したグロピウス・バウのライブプログラムおよびアウトリーチ担当キュレーターのノラ＝スワンチェ・アルメスだ。アマントの広報担当者は6月、準備がすでに進んでいることを 明らかにした 一方、ヴェネチアで使用されたジェットスキーや仮設トイレがブルックリンでも展開されるかどうかについてはついては明言を避けた。この広報担当者はこう続ける。

「ヴェネチアで作品を見た人ならわかると思いますが、この作品は展示場所の特性に応じて内容を調整するものです。ヴェネチア・ビエンナーレ閉幕後、アルメスがどのようにベルリン版を構成するのか。私たちのチームも、それを踏まえた上で具体的に検討することになると思います」

（翻訳：編集部）

Mit ihm verlieren wir einen engagierten Berufskollegen und profunden Kenner der Fotografiegeschichte ebenso wie einen hilfsbereiten, grosszügigen Menschen und guten Freund."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Es gibt Menschen, die mit ihrer Begeisterung, ihrem Wissen und ihrem unermüdlichen Einsatz bleibende Spuren hinterlassen. Heiri Mächler war einer von ihnen. Am 8. März 1955 in Galgenen geboren, galt seine Leidenschaft zeitlebens der Fotografie – und ganz besonders den Menschen, die sich beruflich oder aus persönlichem Interesse mit ihr beschäftigten."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Als Inhaber eines Fotofachgeschäfts in Rüti kannte er die Herausforderungen der Branche aus eigener Erfahrung. Doch Heiri Mächler wollte mehr, als nur seinen eigenen Betrieb erfolgreich führen. article_text:
Die Fotobranche trauert um Heiri Mächler, der am Sonntag, 11. Oktober 2026, im Alter von 71 Jahren völlig unerwartet verstorben ist. Mit ihm verlieren wir einen engagierten Berufskollegen und profunden Kenner der Fotografiegeschichte ebenso wie einen hilfsbereiten, grosszügigen Menschen und guten Freund.

Es gibt Menschen, die mit ihrer Begeisterung, ihrem Wissen und ihrem unermüdlichen Einsatz bleibende Spuren hinterlassen. Heiri Mächler war einer von ihnen. Am 8. März 1955 in Galgenen geboren, galt seine Leidenschaft zeitlebens der Fotografie – und ganz besonders den Menschen, die sich beruflich oder aus persönlichem Interesse mit ihr beschäftigten.

Als Inhaber eines Fotofachgeschäfts in Rüti kannte er die Herausforderungen der Branche aus eigener Erfahrung. Doch Heiri Mächler wollte mehr, als nur seinen eigenen Betrieb erfolgreich führen. Über viele Jahre setzte er sich als Präsident des damaligen Verbands Fotohandel Schweiz (VFS), des heutigen Imagingswiss, für die Interessen seiner Berufskollegen ein. Besonders am Herzen lag ihm die Förderung des Nachwuchses. Er engagierte sich für die Etablierung des Berufs des Fotofinishers und eröffnete damit jungen Menschen neue berufliche Perspektiven. Als Chefexperte in St. Gallen und Mitglied der Schulkommission der Schule für Gestaltung Zürich gab er sein umfangreiches Wissen und seine Erfahrung an die nächste Generation weiter.

Doch Heiri Mächler blickte nicht nur in die Zukunft der Fotografie. Ebenso wichtig war ihm ihre Vergangenheit. Aus seiner Begeisterung für die Fotogeschichte entstand 2012 der Verein Fotohistory, mit dem er sich einer besonderen Aufgabe verschrieb: die Geschichte des Schweizer Fotohandels und seiner technischen Entwicklung für kommende Generationen zu bewahren.

Mit bewundernswerter Ausdauer trug er historische Kameras, Bücher, Dokumente, Kataloge und zahlreiche weitere Zeugnisse der Fotogeschichte zusammen. Daraus entstand eine eindrückliche Sammlung, deren Schätze er im Fotohistory-Museum in Rüti interessierten Besucherinnen und Besuchern zugänglich machte. Wer mit einer Frage zu ihm kam, fand nicht nur einen kompetenten Fachmann, sondern auch einen geduldigen Gesprächspartner, der sein Wissen bereitwillig teilte. Man spürte, dass es ihm nicht allein um alte Kameras und historische Dokumente ging, sondern um die Geschichten und Menschen dahinter.

Unvergessen bleiben auch die zahlreichen Studienreisen, die Heiri Mächler mit grossem organisatorischem Geschick für die Mitglieder von Fotohistory auf die Beine stellte. London, Wien, Paris, Chalon-sur-Saône, Dresden/Wolfen und Lyon waren einige der Stationen, an denen er seinen Mitreisenden die Geschichte der Fotografie näherbrachte. Ebenso wird vielen die von ihm organisierte Feier zum 175-jährigen Bestehen der Fotografie am 19. August 2014 im Kursaal Bern in lebhafter Erinnerung bleiben.

Bei all diesen Aktivitäten zeichnete Heiri Mächler eine Eigenschaft besonders aus: seine selbstverständliche Hilfsbereitschaft. Ob jemand nach einem seltenen fotohistorischen Dokument suchte, eine Auskunft benötigte oder Unterstützung bei einer Recherche wünschte – Heiri nahm sich Zeit. Seine Bereitschaft, für andere da zu sein, beschränkte sich keineswegs auf die Fotografie. Als freiwilliger Rotkreuz-Fahrer begleitete er hilfsbedürftige Menschen und Menschen mit Behinderungen zu ihren Terminen. Auch darin zeigte sich seine menschliche Haltung: helfen, wo Hilfe gebraucht wurde, ohne viel Aufhebens darum zu machen.

Nun ist Heiri Mächler nicht mehr unter uns. Sein plötzlicher Tod macht betroffen und hinterlässt eine schmerzliche Lücke – bei seiner Familie, seinen Kindern und Enkeln, bei seinen Freunden und in der Schweizer Fotobranche.

Was bleibt, ist weit mehr als die Erinnerung an seine beruflichen Verdienste. Es bleibt die Dankbarkeit für einen Menschen, der sich mit Begeisterung und Tatkraft für seine Überzeugungen einsetzte, der Wissen nicht für sich behielt, sondern grosszügig weitergab, und dem das Wohl seiner Mitmenschen stets ein Anliegen war.

Lieber Heiri, wir werden Dich vermissen. Was Du für die Fotografie und für uns alle getan hast, bleibt unvergessen.

Urs Tillmanns

Hinweise:

Die Beerdigun g findet am Samstag, 24. Oktober 2026 um 10:00 Uhr in der Pfarrkirche St. Martin, Kirchweg 1, 8854 Galgenen statt.

article_text:
E XCLUSIVE : The Black List has named the six writers and projects chosen for its 2026 Writers Lab. They are Elton de Almeida ( A Mark of Kin ), Yasmin DeWinter ( Guillaume ), Scott Leddy (Nightwatch) , Marcelle Pallais ( One Last Summer ), Alexander Seltzer and Kyle Jutkiewicz ( Depths ) and Emma Taylor Stock ( Denial ).

The program, now in its 13th year, provides creative mentorship and professional support to promising feature writers as they further develop their selected project during a weeklong workshop in Ojai, CA.

The Black List’s Annual Lab program supports two distinct cohorts: writers and ﬁlmmakers. The Writers Lab focuses on developing feature scripts to be sold in the studio system and/or used as voice samples. The Projects Lab, which will be announced in November, offers writer-directors the chance to develop a screenplay that they intend to direct.

Watch on Deadline

Related Stories

Spiegel & Grau's Full Catalog Available On The Black List Online Platform

Deadline's L.A. Law Summit: Nina Shaw & Patricia Glaser Honored On Day Of Big Ideas, Big Insights; Watch The Video Presentations

During the Lab, each writer will develop their screenplay through peer workshops and one-on-one sessions with working professional screenwriters, including returning mentors Travis Braun ( One Night Only ), Stephany Folsom ( Toy Story 4, The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power ), Katie Silberman ( Set It Up, Don’t Worry Darling ), Victoria Strouse ( Seekers of Infinite Love, Finding Dory ) and Christina Hodson ( Birds of Prey, Bumblebee ).

Black List Annual Lab alumna Savion Einstein ( A Cuban Girl’s Guide To Tea and Tomorrow ) will also join as a session mentor. After the lab concludes, the writers cohort will participate in a yearlong support program involving monthly meetings with screenwriters, agents, managers, producers, and executives. Pitching and peer workshop sessions will be led by Scott Myers ( The Protagonist’s Journey , Spec Script Deals: 1991-2025) who has been a part of every single annual Black List Lab so far.

“We’re excited to welcome the latest cohort of screenwriters to the Black List Lab fold. At a time when the industry can seem particularly challenging and harder than ever to break into, we’re thrilled to be able to support projects that make us excited to go to the movies. These writers are bringing distinctive voices, bold points of view, and stories that deserve to be heard to the Lab and we’re privileged to be able to give them space to take risks, challenge themselves, and build community with other writers, in Ojai and beyond,” said Megan Halpern, Black List SVP.

Submissions for the 2027 Labs are now open on the Black List website .

Previous Black List Lab alumni include Claire Ayoub ( Empire Waist ), Minhal Baig ( We Grown Now ), Tom Dean ( Carolina, Caroline ), Gia Gordon ( Law and Order ), Danny Hogan ( The Pitt ), Jimmy Keyrouz ( Broken Keys ), Dagny Looper ( The Resort) , Alexandra Qin ( ThirstyGirl) , Michelle Steffes ( For When You Get Lost ), and Jason Young ( The Magic Flute) .

Learn more about the 2026 Writers Lab projects, and the creatives behind them, below.

2026 Writers Lab Projects:

Elton de Almeida – A MARK OF KIN

Haunted by her family’s tragic past, a cunning scammer seeks revenge on the uncle who abandoned her decades ago — only to be trapped by a demonic curse that feeds off her bloodline.

Yasmin DeWinter – GUILLAUME

Paris, 1898. Two American brothers walk into a brothel. One vomits on a girl. The other pulls a knife. Within the hour, they owe a madam five thousand francs they don’t have. Their ship sails at dawn. The elder just had a seizure in a piss-soaked alley – and if anyone finds out, he loses his wife, his childen, and his name.

Scott Leddy – NIGHTWATCH

In the midst of an apparent nuclear attack on NATO and the US, a communications blackout with the President places the Defense Secretary in the hot seat on America’s Doomsday Plane, but with the minutes ticking down, a comms expert discovers an anomaly that could change everything.

Marcelle Pallais – ONE LAST SUMMER

A restless, sharp-witted teen aching for meaning and adventure escapes to a wealthy beach town, only to be pulled toward a charming boy and his family’s deadly secret. Adapted from NORTHANGER ABBEY by Jane Austen.

Alexander Seltzer and Kyle Jutkiewicz – DEPTHS

Trapped aboard a US nuclear submarine, a former priest turned navy engineer must stop a demon-possessed Soviet defector before she turns the Cold War hot.

Emma Taylor Stock – DENIAL

When a health insurance giant denies their bestie’s cancer treatment, three friends attempt to approve the claim themselves. But their plan spirals when they accidentally kidnap the CEO and must expose his fraud to save themselves.

title_original: Ceniza en la boca, lo sguardo di Diego Luna su chi cerca una casa lontano da casa
editorial_title_zh: 《Ceniza en la boca》，迭戈·卢纳镜头下那些在远离家乡之处寻找家园的人
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在2026年罗马电影节竞赛单元中，迭戈·卢纳的这部电影呈现了连根拔起、孤独与移民的希望：一份在评判他人之前先去理解的邀请。文章《Ceniza en la boca》，迭戈·卢纳镜头下那些在远离家乡之处寻找家园的人来自……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "有些出发源于希望，最终却近似于一场遗弃。正是在这道裂痕之中，《Ceniza en la boca》展开——这部由迭戈·卢纳执导、改编自布伦达·纳瓦罗同名小说的影片，曾入选戛纳特别展映单元和多伦多电影节，并入围2026年罗马电影节“进步电影”竞赛单元。", "links": [{"text": "Festa del Cinema di Roma 2026", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/festa-del-cinema-di-roma/"}, {"text": "Progressive Cinema", "url": "https://www.romacinemafest.it/it/festa-cinema-roma/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在墨西哥，伊莎贝尔在离开这个国家之前向孩子们露西和迭戈告别。多年后，两个孩子为了追寻更好未来的可能，前往西班牙与她团聚。但跨越一道边境，并不意味着找到家园。马德里显得灰暗、遥远，几乎无力接纳到来者的愿望。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/ceniza-en-la-boca-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "二十一岁的露西不停地做保姆工作，在维持生计的需要、对弟弟的责任，以及依然完整的、想要活出自己青春的需求之间被撕扯。她周围运转着一个要求劳动与随叫随到的世界，却很少追问那些把一切抛在身后之人的疲惫与孤独。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“无论身在何处，都只是活下去而已，”弟弟望着大海对露西说。这句话像一道敞开的伤口贯穿整部影片。因为移民不只是地理上的旅程，更是一道撕裂，波及情感、身份与归属感。母亲曾试图给孩子们一个机会，但她的牺牲以分离为代价。爱与遗弃于是共存，显示出出于必要所做的选择，可能也会在那些本想保护的人身上留下深深的印记。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/ceniza-en-la-boca-4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "迭戈·卢纳避免一切修辞，把移民还原为穿越它之人的面孔。不是数字，不是抽象类别，而是被放弃、痛苦与断裂的纽带所标记的生命。这些人被连根拔离自己的土地、习惯、传统与情感，被迫在常常还未被倾听就已被评判的地方重新开始。影片的政治与人性紧迫性正源于此。在谴责到来者之前，应当试着想象他的故事。我们并不知道那些促使某人出发的伤口、缺失与希望。然而，我们常常忘记那些在我们的家庭和社会中劳作之人的贡献，同时却要求他们融入，却并不真正给予他们空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Ceniza en la boca》邀请人们做出一个简单而困难的举动：设身处地。因为共情不会抹去差异，却能让人认出把我们联结在一起的东西。也因为一个懂得接纳的社会不会失去自己的身份，反而会因新的故事而丰富。在评判之前，必须学会倾听。每一次出发背后，都有一个生命，要求自己不被简化为外来者的处境。", "translated": true}]

Prima di giudicare, occorre imparare ad ascoltare. Dietro ogni partenza c’è una vita che chiede di non essere ridotta alla propria condizione di straniera."}]
article_text:
Ci sono partenze che nascono dalla speranza e finiscono per somigliare a un abbandono. È in questa frattura che si muove Ceniza en la boca , il film di Diego Luna tratto dall’omonimo romanzo di Brenda Navarro , presentato nella sezione Special Screenings di Cannes e al Toronto Film Festival, e in concorso alla Festa del Cinema di Roma 2026 , nella sezione Progressive Cinema .

In Messico, Isabel saluta i figli Lucy e Diego prima di lasciare il Paese. Anni dopo, i due ragazzi la raggiungono in Spagna, inseguendo la possibilità di un futuro migliore. Ma attraversare una frontiera non significa trovare una casa. Madrid appare grigia, distante, quasi incapace di accogliere i desideri di chi arriva.

Lucy, ventunenne, lavora senza sosta come bambinaia, divisa tra la necessità di mantenersi, le responsabilità verso il fratello e il bisogno, ancora intatto, di vivere la propria giovinezza. Intorno a lei si muove un mondo che pretende lavoro e disponibilità, ma raramente si interroga sulla fatica e sulla solitudine di chi ha lasciato tutto alle spalle.

«Ovunque ci si trovi, si tratta solo di sopravvivere», dice il fratello a Lucy guardando il mare. Una frase che attraversa il film come una ferita aperta. Perché la migrazione non è soltanto un viaggio geografico, ma una lacerazione che investe gli affetti, l’identità e il senso di appartenenza. La madre ha cercato di offrire ai figli una possibilità, ma il suo sacrificio ha avuto il prezzo della separazione. L’amore e l’abbandono finiscono così per convivere, mostrando quanto le scelte compiute per necessità possano lasciare segni profondi anche nelle persone che si vorrebbero proteggere.

Diego Luna evita ogni retorica e restituisce alla migrazione il volto di chi la attraversa. Non numeri, non categorie astratte ma esistenze segnate da rinunce, dolori e legami spezzati. Persone sradicate dalla propria terra, dalle abitudini, dalle tradizioni e dagli affetti, costrette a ricominciare in luoghi dove spesso vengono giudicate prima ancora di essere ascoltate. È proprio qui che il film trova la sua urgenza politica e umana. Prima di condannare chi arriva, bisognerebbe provare a immaginare la sua storia. Non conosciamo le ferite, le assenze e le speranze che hanno spinto qualcuno a partire. Eppure, troppo spesso, dimentichiamo il contributo di chi lavora nelle nostre case e nelle nostre società, mentre pretendiamo che si integri senza concedergli davvero uno spazio.

Ceniza en la boca invita a compiere un gesto semplice e difficile, mettersi nei panni degli altri. Perché l’empatia non cancella le differenze, ma permette di riconoscere ciò che ci unisce. E perché una società che sa accogliere non perde la propria identità, ma si arricchisce di nuove storie. Prima di giudicare, occorre imparare ad ascoltare. Dietro ogni partenza c’è una vita che chiede di non essere ridotta alla propria condizione di straniera.
excerpt_original: Sradicamento, solitudine e speranze migranti nel film di Diego Luna in concorso alla Festa del Cinema di Roma 2026: un invito a comprendere l'altro prima di giudicare L'articolo Ceniza en la boca, lo sguardo di Diego Luna su chi cerca una casa lontano da casa proviene da…

article_text:
Each year at Frieze London, Tate gets to buy works on view at the fair through a dedicated fund, and this time around, the museum purchased just two pieces: an abstraction by Michaela Yearwood-Dan and a sculptural work by Luis Fernando Zapata .

Prices were not supplied by Tate, but the Yearwood-Dan painting, titled Peace Unknown (2026), was likely the more expensive work of the two. Sold by the mega-gallery Hauser & Wirth at Frieze London, the painting features bursts of yellow, blue, and green, along with text at the bottom reading: “IF THEY NOT PLAYING BY THE RULES, WHY THE F K ARE WE?” Its surface includes glitter, beads, a ribbon, and paper.

Yearwood-Dan, one of the youngest artists represented by Hauser & Wirth, has had a quick market ascent, with her auction record standing at $880,000. The London-based artist will soon have a New York solo show with Boesky Gallery and is currently the subject of an exhibition at the Whitworth Art Gallery in Manchester, England.

Zapata, by contrast, is less established. The Colombian artist had a relatively short career—he died of AIDS-related causes at age 42 in 1994—and has not had much visibility outside his home country. Yet he has gradually entered museums in the US and Europe, with the Centre Pompidou, the Museo Reina Sofía, the Guggenheim, and others acquiring his art.

Tate bought the 1992 piece Barge from a booth by Galería Elvira Moreno and Alonso Garcés Galería at Frieze Masters, a sister fair that is generally devoted to historical art. Like other works by Zapata, this one is intended to mimic the look of ancient artifacts and is made from papier-mâché.

Neither Yearwood-Dan nor Zapata was previously represented in the Tate collection.

Karin Hindsbo, the interim director of Tate, said in a statement, “The works both represent varied and complex approaches to materiality, evident in the large-scale richly layered surfaces and experimental use of natural and found materials. I look forward to the public being able to enjoy these stunning works in Tate’s galleries and beyond.”

Elsewhere at Frieze, the Contemporary Art Society gave its inaugural artist prize to Okiki Akinfe, whose work was on view at Ginny on Frederick’s booth in the Focus section for emerging galleries. Akinfe won £30,000 (just under $40,000). Ella Fleck, whose work was shown in the Focus section by Ehrlich Steinberg, won the Camden Art Centre Emerging Artist Award; she will now have a show at the titular art museum.

The Contemporary Art Society also spent £100,000 ($132,500) at the fair, acquiring three works: one by Claudia Alarcón and Silät from Proyectos Ultravioleta’s booth; one by Karimah Ashadu, the winner of the Silver Lion at the 2024 Venice Biennale, at Sadie Coles HQ’s booth; and one by Gala Porras-Kim at Sprüth Magers’s booth. All of these works will enter the collection of the Whitworth.

Through its own dedicated Frieze fund, the Arts Council England spent £90,000 ($119,300) to buy works by Armando D. Cosmos, Oliver Osborne, Hannah Quinlan and Rosie Hastings, and Laurie Smith. These works were respectively sold by Phillida Reid, Union Pacific, Arcadia Missa, and Wschód.
excerpt_original: Neither artist was previously represented in the museum network's collection.

article_text:
Nos coups de cœur de la semaine, Carla Lubrano Di Sbaraglione et Remy Badout, photographient les endroits où les silhouettes s’animent. Les corps se touchent et bougent en formant une danse corporelle. Ce qu’on nous transmet ? Beaucoup de sensibilité, de la poésie, de la couleur, sans oublier un fond sonore musical ! Leur univers personnel se dessine sous le regard de lieux habités.

Carla Lubrano Di Sbaraglione

Photographe et vidéaste parisienne, Carla Lubrano Di Sbaraglione photographie les espaces communs, les corps ainsi que les atmosphères qui habitent ces lieux. L’artiste nous confie qu’elle « s’intéresse à ce qui émerge d’une rencontre, à ces instants où quelque chose s’aligne sans avoir été prévu, à ce quelque chose qui se trouve dans la “zone de sincérité” » . Sa liberté se trouve dans les espaces festifs, là où la musique prend vie et où le corps se déchaîne. Son regard artistique est proche du rêve, celui contemplatif et poétique, qui nous emporte loin de la réalité qu’on connaît. Les clichés qu’on observe nous font vivre un événement et celui-ci est rempli de musique. Hypnotisé par les couleurs, le spectateur semble danser lui aussi dans un songe très lointain. Ce qui importe pour l’artiste, c’est l’allure du corps, les silhouettes bougent et vivent encore dans l’image sans y être figées. La photographe nous explique qu’elle « aime les espaces où les identités peuvent bouger, où les corps s’expriment librement et où le collectif devient une forme de soutien » , c’est ce qu’elle essaye de faire exister à travers ses images. Parce que dans son univers rien ne reste dans le passé, ce sont des images qui continuent d’exister. Un baiser, une piste de danse, des corps unis, une foule en mouvement et bien sûr des ombres corporelles qui animent les clichés de l’artiste. Ne croyez pas vous ennuyer en les regardant, ici on danse tout en contemplant !

Remy Badout

Aujourd’hui, la couleur ne manque pas, ce sont des œuvres aux formes et aux géométries diverses qui s’associent. L’artiste Remy Badout nous présente ses œuvres colorées qui s’inspirent du mouvement néo-psychédélique tiré du genre giallo des années 1970. Le giallo est un genre cinématographique et littéraire italien qui mêle cinéma policier, horreur et érotisme. Dans ses clichés les personnages sont intrigants, ils fuient l’image tout en nous provoquant des frissons. Lorsqu’il crée, Remy Badout nous confie qu’il « cherche toujours à contourner la réalité pour révéler constamment une sorte d’onirisme, de rêverie et d’étrange pour voir un mysticisme dans les couleurs » . Son esthétique se relie ici aussi à la musique, celle-ci est à la fois douce et rock, les images défilent devant nos yeux comme une course sans fin. « Mon travail est avant tout obsédé par la texture patinée du souvenir de mon enfance vécue en partie dans une maison typique 60s » , nous dit le photographe. En regardant ses clichés, nous sommes intrigués par la quête de ces silhouettes : pourquoi sont-elles seules au milieu de la nature ? Pourquoi tout est si flou autour de nous ? Les individus photographiés ne ressemblent pas à ceux que nous avons l’habitude de voir, les photos sont « comme des scènes de film ou des cases de BD » , nous rappelle l’artiste. Nous sommes alors convaincus d’une seule chose, nous ne venons pas du même monde !

article_text:
ビデオ・アートの先駆者、飯村隆彦のドキュメンタリーが2027年完成へ。制作支援イベントを東京で開催

ビデオ・アート と 実験映画 の先駆者、 飯村隆彦 の軌跡をたどる日独共同製作のドキュメンタリー『SPEAKING IN IIMURA』。2027年の完成に向け、制作費を募るクラウドファンディングの応援イベントが 東京 ・大森と神田で開催される。

ビデオ・アート と 実験映画 の先駆者、 飯村隆彦 （1937–2022）の軌跡をたどる日独共同製作の長編ドキュメンタリー『SPEAKINGINIIMURA』の2027年の完成に向け、制作費を募るクラウドファンディングの応援イベントが、10月29日に 東京 ・大森、11月14日に神田で開催される。

飯村は1960年代から、 オノ・ヨーコ 、大林宣彦、 赤瀬川原平 、土方巽らとともに、日本のアヴァンギャルド運動の一翼を担った。1960年代後半以降は ニューヨーク やヨーロッパにも活動の場を広げ、 ナム・ジュン・パイク や ジョナス・メカス らと交流した。本作では、東京やニューヨークで構造映画や実験映画に取り組み、ビデオ・アート、ビデオ・インスタレーション、パフォーマンスへと表現領域を広げた飯村の歩みを、本人の言葉や親交のあった人々の証言からひもとく。

制作のきっかけとなったのは、2021年秋の旅行中に飯村が即興で行った、生涯最後とみられるビデオ・パフォーマンスだった。同行した画家の久松知子が偶然持参していたビデオカメラで、飯村自身によって撮影されたもので、彼はその約半年後に亡くなった。2023年にこの映像を見た砂入博史がドキュメンタリーの制作を着想し、翌年に企画が始動。以来、東京、ニューヨーク、ベルリン、パリで関係者へのインタビューを重ねてきた。

2026年2月には、砂入がJ-Docs Hubの支援を受け、ベルリン国際映画祭のフィルムマーケットに参加。ドイツのラピッドアイムービーズ（プロデューサー：ステファン・ホール）との共同製作が決定した。完成後は国内外の映画祭や劇場のほか、美術館や大学での上映も目指している。

制作陣は、監督・共同プロデューサーの砂入と、共同プロデューサーの河合政之、瀧健太郎、久松知子。砂入はニューヨークを拠点に、社会的テーマと個人の記憶を結ぶドキュメンタリーを手がける。ビデオアーティスト・理論家の河合は、1998年から飯村と交流し、著書でもその実践を論じてきた。アーティスト・アーキビストの瀧は、10年以上にわたって飯村の展示活動を支え、「飯村隆彦アーカイブ準備室」の設立を主導している。

制作費を募るクラウドファンディングは、10月10日に MOTION GALLERYで開始 。10月22日時点で35人から約61万円の支援が寄せられている。目標金額は200万円で、募集は2027年1月7日まで。

今回、都内2カ所で開かれる応援イベントでは、未公開映像の試写や制作陣によるトーク、返礼品の紹介、質疑応答、懇談の時間が設けられる。いずれも入場無料で、事前申し込みが必要だ。

『SPEAKINGINIIMURA』クラウドファンディング応援イベント 【第1弾】 会期：10月29日（木） 場所：TAIRU（東京都大田区大森東2-29-5） 時間：19:00〜20:30（開場18:30） 申し込み： https://forms.gle/3gwEw4C8QYJCrZEXA

【第2弾】 会期：11月14日（土） 場所：海老原商店（東京都千代田区神田須田町2丁目13-5） 時間：18:00〜19:30（開場17:30） 申し込み： https://forms.gle/i8FjgP2WdECfmbP69

’Godzilla Minus Zero’, ‘Ramayana’ rule

Godzilla Minus Zero and Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend powered to the top of the global box office ranking this weekend, leading seven new releases, four of them from Asia.

The latest iteration of the venerable Japanese monster franchise claimed the top spot on the Rentrak chart, with Godzilla Minus Zero taking a projected $63m worldwide, according to North American distributor Gkids.

In North America, the sequel claimed an estimated $31.6m, the biggest ever opening for a live action foreign language release, said Gkids.

Internationally, the film got the first simultaneous global launch for a Japanese Godzilla installment (there have also been several recent US-produced entries in the franchise) and took a projected $31.4m from more than 100 territories, including $17m (¥2.7bn) from Japan, where Gkids parent Toho distributed.

The Toho production is a sequel to 2023 franchise installment Godzilla Minus One , with director Takashi Yamazaki and stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Habame and Hidetaka Yoshioka all returning for the story of a Japanese family struggling to recover from the events of the earlier film.

Minus One grossed $114m worldwide and was the first non-English language film to win the visual effects Oscar.

M inus Zero , which premiered at September’s New York festival, was the first ever Japanese production filmed for Imax, and took $21.3m of it global total in Imax venues.

Indian fantasy action-adventure Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend , distributed worldwide excluding India by Sony Pictures, grossed an estimated $52.2m globally over the weekend (for a $55.7m total to date), taking advantage of the Diwali holiday currently being celebrated in India and a number of other countries.

The Hindi language production grossed an estimated $12.2m in North America, Sony reported, and $43.5m from 37 international markets, including $32m from India, where producer Prime Focus distributed.

In the UK, Ramayana broke the opening weekend record for an Indian film with a take of $3m. Other big starts came in the United Arab Emirates, with $2.2m, Australia, with $1.9m, and Germany, with $625,000.

Based on a five-thousand-year-old Sanskrit saga, Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, produced by Namit Malhotra, and stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi in the tale of a prince and an immortal king whose fates are bound by prophecy.

Also filmed for Imax, the three-hour-plus Indian epic took $6m of its global total on Imax screens.

‘The Cat In The Hat’ makes soft start

The biggest of the weekend’s new US films was Warner Bros’ The Cat In The Hat , with an estimated $30.5m worldwide for third place on the chart.

The animated fantasy comedy took $20.5m in North America and $10m from more than 60 international markets. Its top territories were Mexico, with a $1.2m opening, Italy with $1.1m, Spain with $999,000, China with $663,000, Brazil with $541,000 and Colombia with $535,000.

Loosely based on the eponymous Dr Seuss children’s book about a brother and sister visited on a rainy day by the title character, the new film version is written and directed by Alessandro Carloni and has a voice cast led by Bill Hader, Matt Berry and Quinta Brunson.

Universal’s live action version of the Cat In The Hat book, starring Mike Myers, grossed $134m worldwide in 2003, but more recent animated features (all from Universal) based on Dr Seuss characters have produced much bigger numbers: 2012’s The Lorax opened with $70.2m in North America and ended up with $349m worldwide, and 2018’s The Grinch began with $67.6m domestically on its way to $512.7m worldwide.

The new Cat In The Hat, whose performance will be mitigated by a relatively modest reported budget of around $90m, opens in early December in the UK, France and Germany and reaches Japan on December 25 and Australia and New Zealand on December 31.

’Wild Horse Nine’, ‘Drummer Boy’ show promise

Source: Searchlight Pictures

‘Wild Horse Nine’

Another American debutant, Searchlight Pictures’ Wild Horse Nine , distributed by Disney, opened this weekend with an estimated $12.6m worldwide, coming in sixth on the weekend chart.

The awards contender took $6m in North America, giving British-Irish writer-director Martin McDonagh his best opening ever in the territory, and $6.6m internationally. Top markets included the UK, which produced $2m, Italy ($1m), France ($700,000) and Australia ($700,00).

John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell and Steve Buscemi star in the dark comedy about two CIA agents dispatched to Easter island, where they wrestle with their past and present conspiracies.

The film, which premiered in September at Venice before screening at a number of other festivals, opens next week in Germany, Spain and other smaller markets.

A third new US opener, Angel Studios’ Drummer Boy , began its theatrical run with an estimated $9.4m from two territories, for ninth place on the chart, almost all of the take coming from North America.

The musical drama, shot in Ireland, is set during the American Revolutionary War and follows two brothers on opposite sides of the conflict and an enslaved woman.

Joel David Smallbone and Ben Smallbone co-directed, with the former also starring.

‘Stray Kids World Tour’, ‘Scene’ play well

The most impressive debut from the weekend’s other two Asian releases came from Trafalgar Releasing’s Stray Kids World Tour ‘Run It’ Live Viewing, which claimed fourth place on the chart with an estimated $13.9m worldwide.

The musical performance film was beamed live to cinemas in 73 markets on Saturday (November 7) from Japan’s Tokyo Dome, documenting a concert by South Korean boy band Stray Kids.

Indian action comedy Scene came in at seventh on the chart after opening in 17 markets – many also in the midst of Diwali celebrations – to gross $12.5m.

The Tamil language film is directed by Jithu Madhavan and stars Suriya, Nazriya Nazim and Naslen in the story of a police officer forced to reopen an old case with a new team.

article_text:
And how land, material and community identities shift alongside industrial changes

Sitiwinangun , which literally means ‘built land’ ( siti : land and winangun : built), is a village in Cirebon with a long pottery-making tradition dating back to the thirteenth century, shaped by the intersections of Islamic, Arab and Chinese cultures. Central to this legacy is Getak Winangun , a centuries-old paddle-and-anvil pottery-making technique handed down through generations. But this traditional craft has been overshadowed by the used-tyre recycling industry established in the village since the 1970s, which employs many local people. Clay, the raw material for earthenware that used to be harvested from around the village, is also becoming increasingly scarce as residential expansion and industrial activity have restricted access to local deposits. Accordingly, (Mem)Bangun dari Tanah features works by ten artists from Cirebon, Bandung and Makassar who use earth as a material and subject matter to reflect on the Sitiwinangun’s cultural history.

The decline in local pottery-making primarily affects traditional utilitarian earthenware, such as gentong (large storage jars) and pedaringan (earthenware rice-storage vessels), which are increasingly replaced by modern plastic containers as local artisans shift towards industrial labour. Against these disappearing practices of earthenware culture, Remaining of the Abandoned (2025), by Iftikhar A. Rajwie, seeks to preserve fractured memories of the artform. The work takes the form of an angled wall with a freestanding pillar at each end, constructed from stacked terracotta pottery blocks. On each block, the artist presents images of Sitiwinangun’s pottery traditions, incorporating photographs and drawings onto the clay through photocopy transfer and lithography techniques. The images range from portraits of artisans and village landscapes to scattered pottery fragments that have been weathered by time. Collectively they suggest an invitation to the viewer to piece together a narrative of the area’s pottery heritage.

Radi Arwinda and Ramdan Kurnia’s Rupawan: House of the Nine Panakawan (2025) is a series of nine installations that reimagine the adventures of the Punakawan Nine, the (expanded) Cirebon version of the four iconic clown-servant characters in traditional Javanese and Balinese wayang kulit (shadow puppetry). Unlike the standard Javanese roster of four figures, the Cirebon tradition incorporates five additional regional characters, such as Duwala , Bagal Buntung , Ceblok , Bitarota and Sekarpandan , into the comedic ensemble. Five of the nine installations combine terracotta sculptures and wooden elements arranged in houselike structures. The Punakawan figures within them are not in the heavily stylised, traditional wayang kulit aesthetic, but more closely resemble cutesy collectible toys. It’s a fusion of traditional craft and contemporary pop-culture that suggests that the old and new can coexist without friction.

Rajwie’s other work, Neo Heritage (2025), is a series of six earthenware sculptures crafted using smoke-firing techniques that engage with a similar theme. While the sculptures mimic the form of plastic bottles, they are adorned with intricate, traditional Sitiwinangun raised relief motifs, featuring floral patterns, geometric zigzags and hand-carved textures. Here the combination of the persistence of tradition and the impermanence of contemporary life suggests that the meeting of old and new can never be frictionless.

(Mem)Bangun dari Tanah reflects on how land, material and community identities shift alongside industrial changes. As Sitiwinangun’s identity shifts from a traditional potters’ village to an industrial recycling hub, the exhibited works examine how local artisan culture survives these material transformations. By contrasting long-standing Getak Winangun earthenware traditions with industrial forms like plastic bottles and fragmented photo-transfers, these imaginative adaptations of the ceramic tradition show that Sitiwinangun’s local craft heritage is a living, evolving language that is capable of adapting to the realities of modern life – at least in a gallery setting.

(Mem)Bangun dari Tanah was at Sanggar Ikhtiar, Kabupaten Cirebon, 15–20 August

title_original: What could the arrival of Peter Rice at Netflix mean for the streamer’s film culture?

article_text:
Source: Courtesty of Goodfellas

‘La Bola Negra’

Having lavished praise on incoming Netflix chief content officer Peter Rice, co-CEO Ted Sarandos is now expected to get down to business with his shiny new hire to try to change the content culture at the streamer and put an end to what has turned out to be its annus horribilis.

It has been a torrid 10 days at the world’s leading SVoD platform, with the biggest layoffs in the company’s history and a seismic senior executive shuffle capping off a year that has brought a failed merger attempt and a 44% stock plunge.

What has also unsettled Sarandos and co-CEO Greg Peters is the paltry-sounding 2% growth in global engagement in the first half of 2026 (based on a not-paltry-sounding 97 billion hours viewed). That, it turned out, was untenable for a pair of executives who regularly say they want to entertain the entire world and led to Netflix discontinuing its biannual What We Watched report in July.

With hindsight, that was mere tinkering. Last week chief content officer Bela Bajaria was ousted.

There had been rumblings about Bajaria for some months. “Ted had to cut some red meat off the bone as Wall Street has the knives out on the stock, which is in the dumps,” said a producer who has had regular dealings with Netflix. Bajaria, a straight-talking 10-year Netflix veteran, played a large role in building out the international local content strategy. “She could be brutally honest and got to where she was by being incredibly hard-working,” said one source who works in streaming.

Source: Disney

Peter Rice

Enter Rice, the elegant former chairman of Walt Disney Television, chairman of general entertainment for The Walt Disney Company, president of 21st Century Fox, CEO of Fox Networks Group, and president of what was then called Fox Searchlight.

What does this bode for the film culture at Netflix? The UK executive is clearly sharp, well-liked, brings “rare” broad experience, in the words of Sarandos in this week’s earnings call, and “understands talent relations”. That will be critical. David Fincher, Shawn Levy, Stranger Things creators the Duffer Brothers, and Noah Baumbach have not renewed their deals with the streamer, and there will be pressure on the new chief content officer to amass a talent stable.

Not easy. “With Netflix taking criticism for lack of long-term engagement, movies are a harder job than series [to move the dial],” said one producer who has worked with Netflix. Bajaria was a TV person, not a film person, although she championed the service’s most-viewed film of all time KPop Demon Hunters , as well as the upcoming The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth and Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew .

Bajaria worked first with legacy studio whiz Scott Stuber and his diamond-encrusted talent relationships and bloated budgets. Then came Dan Lin, who is leaving after less than three years and had the unenviable task of reining in spend and making the films more broadly appealing (read: amorphous and vanilla but, yes, cheaper). Neither executive secured Netflix the best picture Oscar Sarandos so covets, although watch this space – La Bola Negra is in the race this year.

The consensus in Hollywood is nobody goes to Netflix to watch the films and Sarandos wants to change that. Together with Peters, he went after – and lost – the Warner Bros studios business to bring in IP and raise the bar. Sarandos said this week that the company remains streaming-first; however, the push into more meaningful theatrical releases and box office reporting could set the tone of Rice’s tenure.

“Peter is probably a corporate upgrade on Bela,” said one industry executive. “He commands as much respect in the boardroom as he does with major talent. As Netflix broadens its sphere of activity in entertainment across gaming, verticals, live sports, etc, a seasoned all-rounder like him is the right creative figurehead.”

Who will Rice appoint to lead the film division? Everybody is talking about ex-Warner Bros dynamic duo Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy. They boast top-notch filmmaker relations and could thrive at a well-capitalised studio, although people question the rollercoaster nature of their last few years.

“I have always found Peter to be clever, creative, and thoughtful,” one producer told Screen . “My first thought was whether Ted’s plans are long-term, given Peter’s leadership track record. Might it be an opportunity for a succession plan?”

Studiocanal CEO Anna Marsh outlines group’s film and TV strategy ahead of ‘Ink’, ‘Elsinore’ launches

article_text:
Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s buzzy Elizabeth Holmes doc “ You Can See Everything ” is set to launch into Italy from the Torino Film Festival with the directors expected in tow.

After world premiering in the U.S. at Telluride, and segueing to the New York Film Festival, the doc, which offers an intimate look at the American health-technology company Theranos founder’s life a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors, is launching internationally by hitting the overseas festival circuit, starting with stopovers at Amsterdam’s IDFA documentary festival and the Stockholm International Film Festival in mid-November, followed by Torino.

Related Stories

Jessica Biel Says ‘7th Heaven’ Reboot Will ‘Modernize’ the Show Now That TV Has ‘Less Limitations’: ‘We Were Very Careful About What Our Audience Wanted’

Hugh Hefner's Widow Crystal Harris Asks Jessica Biel to 'Please Reconsider' Playing His Wife: 'I Experienced Sexual, Emotional... Physical Abuse'

“There are films that make me fall in love with cinema all over again and remind me why I’ve dedicated so much of my life to it,” said Torino artistic director Giulio Base in a statement. “You Can See Everything” is one of them: a true masterpiece, bold and unsettling, that turns the boundary between truth and mise-en-scène into a dizzying visual adventure,” the Torino chief added.

Popular on Variety

“You Can See Everything” – which has become one of the year’s biggest box office surprises, opening to a staggering $15.6 million in the U.S., followed by a spectacular $19.5 million in its second frame this past weekend – is being released in Italy by Andrea Romeo’s I Wonder Pictures which is one of the country’s top distributors and has close ties to A24.

“You Can See Everything” will hit cinemas in the U.K. and Ireland on Nov. 20 with A24 is self-releasing the film. Sony Pictures Worldwide has acquired distribution rights for Latin America, Scandinavia, South Africa, Germany, Austria, Greece, the Middle East, Israel, India, South Korea and Southeast Asia, with specific dates to be announced soon.

I Wonder has also not yet set an Italian release date for the film. The 44th edition of the Torino Film Festival, the third under Base’s guidance, is set to take place in Turin from Nov. 24 to Dec. 2, 2026.

The Torino Film Festival’s full lineup will be announced on Thursday.

鳥を導く

劇場公開日： 2026年10月31日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

U-NEXTで 関連作品を見る PR

解説・あらすじ

PFFアワード2017入選作品「やさしいフルスイング」の尾崎健監督の長編2作目にして劇場初公開作。スランプに陥った音楽家の青年が、懐かしい思い出に満ちた山奥で自分自身と向き合いながら再生していく姿を描く。 東京に住む晴太は、広告で使用される音楽を作って生計を立てている。ある日、「自由に音楽を作って欲しい」という依頼を受けるが、納得のいく音楽が思い浮かばずスランプに陥ってしまう。落ち込んだ晴太は行方をくらまし、幼い頃に家族と過ごした山奥のペンションを訪れる。ひとりきりで音楽と向き合う彼は、鳥の鳴き声に魅了され、それを録音することに夢中になっていく。そこへ、マイペースでパワフルなろう者の姉・あずみが姿を現す。 主人公・晴太を演じるのは、本作が映画初主演となる稲川悟史。ろう者の両親のもとで育ったルーツをもつ稲川が、手話の監修や指導も担った。晴太の姉・あずみ役で「やさしいフルスイング」にも出演した田中志朋、あずみのパートナー・太一役で「沈没家族」など監督としても活動する加納土が共演。本作の制作は、稲川と田中という2人の俳優がこれまで学ぶことのなかった技術を体得し作品へ昇華させることをテーマに置いて進められ、稲川は「音楽」、田中は「手話」を選択。この2つの要素を取り入れた脚本を尾崎監督が執筆し、3年の制作期間を経て完成させた。

2024年製作／78分／日本 劇場公開日：2026年10月31日

article_text:
横須賀美術館（神奈川県横須賀市）で、「生誕120年 三岸節子展」が11月14日から開催されます。

戦後日本を代表する画家のひとり、三岸節子は、1905年、現在の愛知県一宮市に生まれました。夫・三岸好太郎の早逝や、戦争の惨禍を乗り越えて描き続け、1950年代には、日本を代表する画家として高い評価を受けました。1954年に初めてフランスを訪れ、のちには南フランスのカーニュや、ブルゴーニュ地方のヴェロンを拠点として、深い色彩と力強い造形による独自の風景画を完成させました。国内では1964年に、陽光のゆたかな神奈川県大磯にアトリエを設け、晩年まで旺盛に制作を続けました。

本展では、美術史家・山田諭氏の監修のもと、一宮市三岸節子記念美術館の所蔵作品を中心に、初出品となる作品を含む約70点が年代順に紹介されます。初期から晩年までの代表的な作品を通じて、「情熱の画家」三岸節子が生涯にわたって展開した芸術を見ることができます。

生誕120年 三岸節子展

会場：横須賀美術館 企画展示室（神奈川県横須賀市鴨居4-1）

会期：2026年11月14日（土）～12月20日（日）

開館時間：10:00～18:00

休館日：12/7（月）

観覧料：一般1,500円、高大生・65歳以上1,300円 ※市内在住・在学の高校生は無料 ※中学生以下無料 ※身体障害者手帳・療育手帳、精神障害者保健福祉手帳をお持ちの方と付添の方1名様は無料

アクセス： ・京急線「馬堀海岸」駅もしくはJR「横須賀」駅から観音崎行バス「ラビスタ横須賀観音崎テラス・横須賀美術館前」下車徒歩2分（京急線「浦賀」駅から観音崎行バス終点「観音崎」下車徒歩5分） ・横浜横須賀道路馬堀海岸I.C.から約3km（約5分）

詳細は、 横須賀美術館公式サイト まで。

見どころ1 代表作70点による本格的回顧展

1920年代から画家として活動した三岸節子。1950年代には、薫り高い色彩と華麗な造形による静物画が人気を博し、第1回サンパウロ・ビエンナーレや、第8回サロン・ド・メといった国際的な展覧会に出品します。その後、南フランスのカーニュや、神奈川県の大磯を拠点として、独自の風景画に取り組み、1999年に94歳の生涯を全うするまで、日本を代表する画家として活躍しました。本展は、三岸節子の代表的な作品70点を、7つの章に分けて構成し、70年以上にわたる画業の展開を見ることができる本格的な回顧展です。

見どころ2 地域交流プログラム

本展は、一宮市三岸節子記念美術館、神戸市立小磯記念美術館、横須賀美術館の連携により開催されています。3館協働による「地域交流プログラム」として、各館の近隣にある「節子ゆかりの風景」を学芸員が取材した映像（スライドショー）の上映、来場者が詠んだ短歌を掲示する「三岸節子を詠む」が実施されます。

激動の時代を駆け抜け、94歳で天寿を全うするまでカンヴァスに向かい続けた「情熱の画家」三岸節子。夫・好太郎との死別や戦禍といった数々の試練に直面しながらも、ひたむきに絵筆を握り続けたその生涯は、見る者に深い勇気と感動を与えてくれます。本展では、若き日の鋭いまなざしを捉えた初期作から、ヨーロッパの空気感を力強い筆致と鮮烈な色彩で表現した円熟期の風景画、そして最晩年に生命の輝きを描ききった傑作まで、70年を超える画業の全貌が一堂に会します。彼女が魂を注ぎ込んだ色彩のきらめきと不屈の芸術精神を、ぜひ会場で体感してみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
Sales agency The Playmaker Munich has closed distribution deals for the animated movie “The Unicorn That Said No” in several territories, ahead of its market premiere at the American Film Market in Los Angeles.

The feature has been sold to Unlimited Media for the Baltic states, WWE Rights for Benelux, KMBO for France, Grand Entertainment for Motion Pictures for the Middle East, M2 Films for Poland, Idea Film for Romania, Another World Entertainment for Scandinavia, Pack Magic for Spain and Orjinlab for Turkey.

Related Stories

Acrobatic Pastor’s Secret Obsession Drives Boo Junfeng’s ‘Trinity’ at Tokyo Gap-Financing Market

'Mother Bhumi,' 'Rehana Maryam Noor' and 'The Tourist' Producers Head to Indonesia’s JAFF Market for New Exchange Program

The German distributor is Warner Bros. Film Productions Germany, with a release on Jan. 1, 2027.

“The Unicorn That Said No” is based on the book “Das Neinhorn” by Marc-Uwe Kling and Astrid Henn, which has been translated into more than 25 languages.

The movie centers on a “sweet, grumpy unicorn” who can no longer bear the pink, idyllic world of his unicorn family and sets off for Nowhere. He unexpectedly finds new friends and together they must rescue the king’s daughter from her tower in order to return home with his new gang.

The movie is directed by Kling, Johannes Weiland (“The Gruffalo’s Child”) and Studio Soi, with a screenplay by Kling and Marcus Sauermann.

Kling also lends his voice to the unicorn. The German voice cast also features Nora Tschirner, Torsten Sträter and Karoline Herfurth.

The movie is a production of X Filme Creative Pool (“Run Lola Run,” “Goodbye, Lenin!”) and Studio Soi (“The Gruffalo,” “The Wonderfully Weird World of Gumball”), in co-production with Warner Bros. Film Productions Germany. Producers are Uwe Schott, Nicole Kellerhals and Carsten Bunte. Co-producers are Steffen Schier, Margret Mackuth and Julia Hayungs. Music is by Felix Raffel, and the main song is by Dota Kehr.

The movie is supported by MFG, MDM, BKM, FFA and Kuratorium Junger Deutscher Film.

The market premiere will be at 11 a.m. on Nov. 11 at AMC Century City in Los Angeles. The Playmaker Munich will be based at the Fairmont Century Plaza, Los Angeles during AFM .

Sylvia Edelmann, head of sales at The Playmaker, said, “It’s wonderful to see so many territories on board before the film has even screened. The book is a hit with readers of all ages around the world, and we can’t wait to bring this sweet, grumpy unicorn to even more audiences at AFM.”

title_original: Florentina Holzinger Is Closing Out ‘Seaworld Venice’ With a ‘Final Dinner’ Made From Bodily Waste
editorial_title_zh: Florentina Holzinger将以一场用身体排泄物制作的“最后晚餐”为“威尼斯海洋世界”闭幕
editorial_excerpt_zh: 公告中写道：“蒸馏后的残余物包含了过去七个月里从展馆访客收集的所有身体排泄物，它将作为一座面向未来的纪念碑。”
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在钢琴术语中，练习曲（étude）是一首技巧上较为棘手的乐曲，通常用于练习，以突破音乐家的极限。顺着这个逻辑，Florentina Holzinger在威尼斯双年展的最后一场表演名为《CLOSING É TUDE》，这表明在她那颠覆礼法、充满废弃物的奇境《SEAWORLD VENICE》持续七个月之后，前方仍有耐力极限的壮举等待着她。", "links": [{"text": "Florentina Holzinger", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/florentina-holzinger/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "兼具表演与装置性质的《SEAWORLD VENICE》于5月在奥地利国家馆开幕，伴随着从威尼斯潟湖打捞上来的一口巨大古钟刺耳的鸣响。契合她以身体为先的哲学，全裸的Holzinger充当了这口钟的人形撞锤。这口巨钟在没有艺术家的陪伴下，继续记录着时间的流逝，每个小时都在展馆及其宾客上方敲响，犹如一座献给正在上演的威尼斯末日场景的荒诞祭坛。人类的排泄物（新鲜采集的）和潟湖废弃物——那种偶尔随涨潮冲上岸的东西——构成了她装置的材料。参观者被鼓励使用现场的移动厕所；尿液则被过滤到一个水牢（dunk tank）中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了《CLOSING É TUDE》，这口巨钟将通过一场仪式感十足的游行，从展馆移至威尼斯卡纳雷吉欧（Cannaregio）区的历史建筑仁慈大会堂（Scuola Grande della Misericordia）。该建筑在中世纪作为行会创立，在经过建筑修复后于2015年作为展览空间重新开放。高耸的天花板、深邃的空间以及壁画（归属于保罗·委罗内塞〔Paolo Veronese〕画派）与这口钟及其所奠定的神圣基调相得益彰。唤起对基督的联想，《CLOSING É TUDE》是一场“最后的晚餐”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "根据公告，“这最后一场威尼斯练习曲追溯了从固体到液体的物质转变，铸就了一件圣物。蒸馏后的残余物包含了过去七个月里从展馆访客收集的所有身体排泄物，它将作为一座面向未来的纪念碑，于11月22日在关闭的展馆前呈现。”当钟声“归于寂静”且水流“停止循环”时，展览即告结束。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个展览很快将以崭新的面貌重生。《SEAWORLD VENICE》的改编版本将于明年春天在柏林的格罗皮乌斯建筑展（Gropius Bau）呈现，接着于那年秋天在维也纳艺术馆（Kunsthalle Wien）停留，随后于2028年3月在布鲁克林的Amant迎来其最后一站。", "links": [{"text": "Amant", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/amant/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾组织威尼斯展出的格罗皮乌斯建筑展现场项目与推广策展人Nora-Swantje Almes将负责监督这一全新版本的迭代。Amant的一位发言人6月向《ARTnews》证实，相关筹备工作已经展开，但拒绝确认来自威尼斯的摩托艇和移动厕所是否会一同运往那里。“如果你看过威尼斯的那场展览，就会知道它对场地的呼应非常强，因此[Almes]需要弄清楚在威尼斯双年展于今秋闭幕后，如何将其改编以适应柏林，”该发言人说，“在那之后，我们将更好地了解我们自己的团队如何进一步为布鲁克林对其进行改编。”", "links": [{"text": "confirmed", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/after-venice-florentina-holzingers-sea-world-coming-brooklyn-1234790163/"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
In piano parlance, an étude is a technically tricky piece of music typically practiced to push a musician beyond their limits. Following that logic, the name of Florentina Holzinger ’s final Venice Biennale performance, CLOSING É TUDE , suggests that after seven months of her propriety-imploding, waste-wonderland SEAWORLD VENICE , there are feats of endurance still ahead.

Part performance, part installation, SEAWORLD VENICE opened at the Austrian Pavilion in May with the piercing peal of a colossal bell salvaged from the Venice Lagoon. In line with her body-first philosophy, a nude Holzinger served as its human clapper. The bell, sans artist, continues to mark the passage of time, ringing every hour over the pavilion and its guests, a grotesque altar to the ongoing Venetian apocalypse. Human refuse (freshly sourced) and lagoon waste, the sort that occasionally washes in with the high tide, form the material of her installation. Visitors were encouraged to use port-a-potties on site; the urine was filtered into a dunk tank.

For CLOSING É TUDE , the bell will travel in a ceremonial procession from the pavilion to the Scuola Grande della Misericordia, a historic building in Venice’s Cannaregio district. Founded in the Middle Ages as a guild, the building reopened as an exhibition space in 2015 after an architectural restoration. A soaring ceiling, a cavernous belly, and frescoes (attributed to the school of Paolo Veronese) suit the bell and the sacred tone she’s struck. Conjuring shades of Christ, CLOSING É TUDE is “a final dinner.”

According to the announcement, “This last Venice Étude traces a material transformation from solid to liquid, forging a relic. Containing all the bodily waste collected from pavilion visitors over the past seven months, the distilled remains serve as a monument for the future, which will be presented in front of the closed pavilion on November 22.” The show ends when the bell “falls silent” and water “stops circulating.”

The show is born anew, soon enough. An adapted version of SEAWORLD VENICE will be presented at Gropius Bau in Berlin next spring, followed by a stop at Kunsthalle Wien in Vienna that fall, before its last leg in March 2028 at Amant in Brooklyn.

Nora-Swantje Almes, curator for live programs and outreach at Gropius Bau, who organized the Venice presentation, will oversee this new iteration. A spokesperson for Amant confirmed to ARTnews in June that preparations were already underway, but declined to confirm whether the jet skis and porta-potties from Venice will make the trip. “If you saw the show in Venice, you know it’s very site-responsive, so [Almes] needs to figure out how to adapt it for Berlin after the Biennale closes in Venice this fall,” the spokesperson said. “After that, we’ll have a better idea of how our own team can further adapt it for Brooklyn.”
excerpt_original: "Containing all the bodily waste collected from pavilion visitors over the past seven months, the distilled remains serve as a monument for the future," reads the announcement.

article_text:
パナソニック汐留美術館（東京都港区）から、2027年の展覧会スケジュールが発表されました。2027年は、「スウェーデンのうつわ グスタフスベリのある暮らし」「ひろしま美術館コレクション 美の交響 ―フランス近代美術と日本洋画の100年―」「Dancing Bauhaus, Beyond 踊るバウハウス、その先へ〔仮〕」「女性建築家をテーマとした建築展（タイトル未定）」と、全部で4つの展覧会が予定されています。

北欧デザインの巨匠たちによる陶磁器をはじめ、セザンヌやモネなど巨匠たちの響き合い、身体と空間を問うバウハウスの展開まで多彩な企画が並び、常設のルオー・ギャラリーとともに見ごたえあるラインナップです。そこでここまで判明した各展覧会の概要について、それぞれまとめました。

パナソニック汐留美術館

所在地：東京都港区東新橋1-5-1 パナソニック東京汐留ビル4階

開館時間：午前10時～午後6時、夜間開館日は午後8時まで（入館は30分前まで）

休館日：水曜日（ただし祝日と会期最終週は開館）、展示替期間、年末年始、夏季休業期間

観覧料：一般1200円、65歳以上1100円、大学生・高校生700円 ※中学生以下無料 ※展覧会によって入館料が異なる場合あり ※障がい者手帳またはミライロIDをご提示の方、および付添者1名まで無料で入館可能

アクセス： JR「新橋」駅より徒歩約8分 東京メトロ銀座・都営浅草線・ゆりかもめ「新橋」駅より徒歩約6分 都営大江戸線「汐留」駅より徒歩約5分

詳細は、 パナソニック汐留美術館公式サイト まで。

スウェーデンのうつわ グスタフスベリのある暮らし

2027年1月16日～3月22日

1825年に設立された、スウェーデンを代表する陶磁器メーカーであるグスタフスベリの全貌を日本で初めて紹介する展覧会です。そのデザインは時代を越えて愛され続け、今日においてもスウェーデンと北欧の応用美術産業と、デザイン史において重要な位置を占めてきました。

グスタフスベリの代表的な4人の陶芸家でデザイナーである、ヴィルヘルム・コーゲ、スティグ・リンドベリ、リサ・ラーソン、カーリン・ビョルクヴィストに焦点をあて、スウェーデン国立美術館所蔵の約300点で、それぞれの個性と創造性が織りなすグスタフスベリの豊かな世界を堪能することができます。

空間演出を担当するのは、 スウェーデン王立工科大学への留学を経験した浅子雄祐（SPROUTZ Studio）。スウェーデンの食卓やくつろぎの時間と深く結びつく「光」をテーマとした展示空間にも要注目です。

ひろしま美術館コレクション 美の交響 ―フランス近代美術と日本洋画の100年―

2027年4月10日～6月20日

19世紀半ばから20世紀前半にかけて、フランス美術は旧来の伝統から離れ、新たな美の基準を次々と切り拓く大きな変革を遂げました。こうした西洋近代美術の動向は、一定の時間差を伴いながら日本へと伝わります。しかし日本の洋画家たちは、単なる西洋美術の受容や模倣にとどまらずに独自の油彩画の表現を築き上げました。

本展は、国内屈指のフランス近代美術のコレクションを誇るひろしま美術館の名品によって、バルビゾン派からエコール・ド・パリに至るフランス近代美術の革新の歩みをたどり、その創造のダイナミズムに迫ります。モネ、セザンヌ、ゴーギャン、マティス、黒田清輝、安井曾太郎。絵画に革新をもたらした巨匠たちの名品が集結。フランス絵画と日本近代洋画の傑作が同一空間に配置され、フランスと日本それぞれの造形をめぐる探究の対比と、作品同士の国境を越えた響き合いを楽しむことができるでしょう。

同館のコレクションが東京での大規模に紹介されるのはじつに45年ぶり。ファン必見の絵画展となりそうです。

Dancing Bauhaus, Beyond 踊るバウハウス、その先へ〔仮〕

2027年7月15日～9月23日

20世紀の芸術・デザイン史に大きな転換をもたらしたバウハウスを起点に、その理念と実践が現代の造形文化のなかでどのように継承され、展開してきたのかが紹介されます。

本展は武蔵野美術大学 美術館・図書館との二館共同企画として開催され、同館がオスカー・シュレンマーの創作活動を総合的に紹介するのに対し、パナソニック汐留美術館ではその視点を受け継ぎながら、「身体と空間」という主題に着目します。絵画、グラフィック、工芸、建築・インテリアなどを通して、芸術と技術の新たな関係を模索したバウハウスの思想と活動を再考するとともに、エットレ・ソットサス、倉俣史朗、三宅一生らの実践を通して、バウハウスの理念が身体と空間、そして生活をめぐる造形思考のなかでいかに継承され、新たなかたちへと展開してきたのかを読み解きます。

女性建築家をテーマとした建築展

2027年10月16日～12月19日

秋は女性建築家をテーマとした建築展が開催されます。詳細は追って発表される予定です。

北欧スウェーデンの暮らしを彩ってきたグスタフスベリの陶芸デザインから、名門・ひろしま美術館のコレクションが織りなすフランス近代美術と日本洋画の対話、そして現代の造形思考へと受け継がれるバウハウスの革新的な展開、秋に予定されている注目の女性建築家展まで、2027年も多彩で魅力あふれる展示が揃いました。世界で唯一の常設展示室であるルオー・ギャラリーとあわせ、ぜひ足を運んでみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

美術展ナビ×国立能楽堂コラボとして、マンガ家の朔野安子さんによる、能や狂言のストーリーを分かりやすく紹介してもらうマンガ連載。今回は、狂言の「 呼声 」です。無断欠勤の太郎冠者の家に、主人たちが訪れます。太郎冠者は居留守でごまかそうとしますが………。

12月に「呼声」を見てみませんか！

国立能楽堂では12月普及公演「呼声・巻絹」が行われます。

公演期間 2026年12月12日（土） 開演時間 午後1時開演 ※開場時間は開演の1時間前の予定

解説・能楽あんない 狂言 呼声 大藏基誠（大蔵流） 能 巻絹 粟谷明生（喜多流） 正面＝5,800円 脇正面＝4,000円（学生2,800円） 中正面＝3,500円（学生2,500円） チケットは電話・ インターネット 予約（11月10日午前10時から）で。 詳しくは、 国立能楽堂の公式サイト で。
